newsitem.title: INDIA: Foreign institutional investment in India rises.
newsitem.headline: Foreign institutional investment in India rises.

text.p: Finance Minister P. Chidambaram said on Thursday that foreign institutional investors (FIIs) invested $2.39 billion in 1996/97 (April-March) in India compared with $2.04 billion in the previous year.

"The government has taken various steps to attract foreign investments particularly with a view to achieving in future the target in the Common Minimum Programme (CMP) of an annual foreign direct investment inflow of $10 billion," Chidambaram informed the upper house of the parliament.
The CMP is a policy blueprint of the ruling United Front coalition unveiled last year after it assumed office in June.
